create.title: Create container
create.notesTitle: Some settings of the original are not carried over:

f.name: Name
f.publishAll: Publish all exposed ports on free ports

h.name: Optional: if empty, Docker generates one.
h.image: Must exist on this computer (pulling arrives in phase 4).
h.argv: Split into arguments with shell-style quoting, but no shell is run.
h.entrypointMulti: Docker accepts a single executable in --entrypoint: the remaining items are sent at the start of the command.
h.volumeName: Empty = anonymous volume. Docker creates it if it doesn't exist.
h.user: Name or UID[:GID]. Empty = image default.
h.image_remote: It must exist on the server.

g.processHint: What runs when the container starts.
g.envHint: Values of keys such as PASSWORD or TOKEN are hidden on screen, but they are sent to Docker as-is and anyone with Docker access can read them.
g.portsHint: Publish container ports on this computer.
g.mountsHint: Docker volumes or folders on this computer (bind mounts).
g.restartHint: What Docker does when the main process exits.
g.capsHint: Comma separated, e.g. NET_ADMIN or ALL.
g.mountsHint_remote: Docker volumes or server folders (bind mounts).
g.portsHint_remote: Publish container ports on the server.

create.imageVolumes: The image declares volumes at {{paths}}. If you mount nothing there, Docker creates anonymous volumes.
create.imageNotLocal: Image {{ref}} is not on this computer. Docker won't pull it when creating the container; pull it first (phase 4) or choose a local one.
create.imageDefaultsError: Could not read the image configuration: {{message}}
create.equivalentHint: Equivalent Docker CLI command. The app doesn't run it: it sends the request to the API and records it in the activity panel.
create.bodyHint: Body of POST /containers/create that will be sent to Docker.
create.startFailed: The container was created but could not be started: {{message}}
create.secretsHidden_one: {{count}} sensitive value is shown as ******** here and in the activity panel; Docker receives it in full.
create.secretsHidden_other: {{count}} sensitive values are shown as ******** here and in the activity panel; Docker receives them in full.
create.imageNotLocal_remote: Image {{ref}} is not on the server. Docker will not download it when creating the container; pull it on this server first or choose one it already has.

name.invalid: Invalid name: use letters, digits, “_”, “.” or “-”, starting with a letter or digit.
name.backupReserved: That name is reserved for backups (“-dcc-backup-”, “-dcc-replaced-”).
name.inUse: Another container already has that name.

argv.trailingEscape: Ends with a backslash with nothing after it.

path.notAbsolute: Must be an absolute path (start with /).

env.duplicate: {{key}} is repeated; the last value wins.

ports.ignoredWithNetwork: With the “{{network}}” network Docker ignores published ports.

port.privileged: Port {{port}} is privileged: it may fail with rootless Docker.
port.inUseByContainer: Port {{port}} is already published by the running container {{container}}.

mount.targetInvalid: The container path must be absolute and not /.
mount.targetDuplicate: There is already a mount at {{target}}.

volume.nameRequired: A new volume needs a name: an anonymous one could not be mounted again in a later recreation.

bind.missing: Folder {{path}} does not exist on this computer.
bind.sensitive: Mounting {{path}} writable gives the container control over the system. Mark it read-only if you don't need writes.
bind.missing_remote: Folder {{path}} does not exist on the server.

cpus.range: Enter a number of CPUs between 0.01 and 1024.

memory.reservationAboveLimit: The reservation cannot exceed the limit.

autoRemove.restart: “Remove when it exits” is not compatible with a restart policy.

issues.privileged: Privileged mode gives the container almost full access to the computer.

ref.invalidRepository: Invalid name: lowercase letters, digits and the separators . _ - only
ref.invalidTag: Invalid tag: letters, digits, _ . - (128 max, not starting with . or -).

context.huge: Using {{path}} as context would send a huge number of files.

dockerfile.invalid: Invalid path: it must be relative and inside the context.
dockerfile.missing: {{path}} does not exist in the context folder.

tags.none: Without a name, the image will show as <none>.

arg.secret: {{key}} looks like a secret: arguments stay in the image history.

driver.singleton: There can only be one network with the {{value}} driver (the predefined one).
driver.swarm: Overlay networks require Docker Swarm: without it, Docker will reject the creation.
driver.noParent: Without the "parent" option, the network has no way out through any physical interface.

subnet.required: Set the subnet to use a gateway or range.
subnet.hostBits: {{value}} is not a network address; it should be {{fixed}}.
subnet.family: {{value}} is not of this address family.

gateway.family: {{value}} is not of this address family.

ipRange.hostBits: {{value}} is not a network address; it should be {{fixed}}.
ipRange.family: {{value}} is not of this address family.

ipv6.disabled: Enable IPv6 to use an IPv6 subnet.

volumeName.short: The name must have at least two characters.
volumeName.invalid: Invalid name: use letters, digits, "_", "." or "-", starting with a letter or digit.
volumeName.exists: A volume named {{value}} already exists. Docker would return the existing one without applying these changes.

volumeOpt.unknownLocal: The local driver only uses type, device and o: "{{key}}" will be sent anyway.
volumeOpt.deviceWithoutType: "device" usually needs "type" (e.g. none with o=bind, nfs or tmpfs).

edit.numberInvalid: Enter a number greater than zero or leave the field empty.

commit.repositoryInvalid: Invalid repository: lowercase letters, digits and the separators “.”, “_”, “-” and “/” (e.g. my-app or registry.local:5000/team/app).
commit.tagInvalid: Invalid tag: letters, digits, “_”, “.” and “-”, up to 128 characters, not starting with “.” or “-”.
commit.controlChars: It cannot contain line breaks or other control characters.

risk.runtimeSocket: {{path}}: the container engine socket gives full control of Docker and, through it, of the host. Mounting it read-only does not prevent this.
risk.hostRoot: Mounting the system root (/) gives the container access to every file on the host.
risk.credentials: {{path}} contains credentials of the host or its users (passwords, SSH keys, tokens), even when mounted read-only.
risk.systemDir: {{path}} is a system folder: the container can read it and, with write access, change how the host works.
risk.systemBinaries: {{path}} with write access lets the container replace programs or libraries on the host.
risk.capability: Capability {{cap}}: extends what the container can do with the host kernel.
risk.privileged: Privileged mode: the container gets almost full access to the host (devices, kernel and all capabilities).
risk.networkHost: Host network: the container sees every service on the host, including those that only listen on 127.0.0.1.
risk.hostNamespace: Shares the {{namespace}} namespace with the host: the container can see (and sometimes affect) the host's processes, shared memory or configuration.
risk.securityOpt: {{option}} turns off a kernel protection ({{protection}}) that limits what the container can do on the host.
risk.device: Device {{device}}: the container accesses that host device directly, bypassing file permissions.
risk.cgroupParent: Custom control group ({{parent}}): the container is placed outside the limits Docker manages.
risk.portAllInterfaces: Port {{port}} is published on all interfaces: other machines on the network can connect and, with Docker, the firewall (UFW, firewalld) usually does not block it. Use 127.0.0.1 if you only need it on this computer.

dupNotes.composeLabels: Compose labels were removed: the duplicate won't belong to the project.
dupNotes.portsConflict: The same host ports are in use by the original; change them or stop the original before starting.
dupNotes.mountTypeUnsupported: There are mounts of a type the wizard doesn't support (tmpfs, npipe…).
dupNotes.namedVolumesShared: Named volumes are shared with the original, not copied.
dupNotes.extraNetworks: Only the first network is connected; the others are not carried over.
dupNotes.dns: DNS settings are not carried over.
dupNotes.securityOpt: Security options (--security-opt) are not carried over.
dupNotes.tmpfs: tmpfs mounts are not carried over.
dupNotes.cpuset: Pinned CPUs (--cpuset-cpus) are not carried over.
dupNotes.pidsLimit: The process limit is not carried over.
dupNotes.logConfig: Logging configuration is not carried over.
dupNotes.healthcheck: The custom health check is not carried over.
dupNotes.stopSignal: The custom stop signal is not carried over.
dupNotes.imageMissing: The original image is no longer on this computer: its defaults could not be separated.

pull.referenceHint: Name with optional tag: nginx:1.27, user/app, registry.example.com:5000/app:v2. Without a tag, latest is used.

authHint.dockerConfig: Like docker pull: uses the credentials saved with docker login (or its credential helper), if there are any for that registry.
authHint.manual: For this pull only: they are not saved anywhere and don't appear in the activity panel.

pull.shareLocal: Send this computer's registry credentials to the server “{{server}}”
pull.shareLocalOn: The docker login credentials of this computer will be used for that registry, and the server will be able to see them.
pull.shareLocalOff: Unchecked, the download on the server is anonymous: this computer's credentials never leave it.

imageDetail.layersSummary_other: {{count}} history entries, {{data}} with data, {{size}} in total.
imageDetail.inspectHint: Full output of docker image inspect {{name}}, exactly as Docker returns it.

imageOps.repositoryHint: For example myapp, user/myapp or registry.example.com:5000/myapp.
imageOps.removeTagBody: This tag is removed. If it is the only one, Docker also removes the image and its unused layers.
imageOps.removeImageBody: The image and the layers no other image uses are removed. This cannot be undone: you would have to pull or build it again.
imageOps.runningRefuses: Docker won't remove an image used by a running container, even when forced: stop and remove it first.
imageOps.stoppedNeedForce: Removing it requires forcing; the containers will still exist, but without their image you won't be able to recreate them.
imageOps.forceMulti: Needed to remove an image with several tags (--force).
imageOps.forceUsed: Needed because stopped containers use it (--force).
imageOps.removed: {{untagged}} tags removed and {{deleted}} layers or images deleted.
imageOps.pruneDangling: Only untagged images no container uses
imageOps.pruneAll: All images no container uses, including tagged ones
imageOps.pruneEstimate_one: Based on the current list, {{count}} image would be removed ({{size}}).
imageOps.pruneEstimate_other: Based on the current list, {{count}} images would be removed ({{size}}).
imageOps.pruneNote: Docker makes the final decision and also removes the related build cache. This cannot be undone.
imageOps.pruneSure: I understand I will have to pull or build those images again
imageOps.pruneWhilePulling_one: {{count}} download is in progress. Wait for it to finish: with the containerd image store, Docker makes ongoing downloads fail when pruning.
imageOps.pruneWhilePulling_other: {{count}} downloads are in progress. Wait for them to finish: with the containerd image store, Docker makes ongoing downloads fail when pruning.

build.special_other: {{count}} special files (sockets, devices or FIFOs) are not sent.

build.bigContext: The context is large: consider excluding folders with .dockerignore.

networks.loadError: Could not get the network list: {{message}}

netOps.runningBlocks_other: {{count}} running containers are connected: Docker will not remove the network until you disconnect or stop them.
netOps.stoppedBreak_one: {{count}} stopped container has this network configured. Docker removes it anyway and that container will not start until you disconnect it or recreate the network:
netOps.stoppedBreak_other: {{count}} stopped containers have this network configured. Docker removes it anyway and those containers will not start until you disconnect them or recreate the network:

netOps.pruneEstimate_other: According to the current list, {{count}} networks will be removed:

composeList.intro: Projects with containers in Docker (detected by their labels) and the ones you add to the list. Every operation runs the official Docker Compose and is recorded in the activity panel with the exact command.
composeList.search: Search by name, folder or service
composeList.loadError: Could not get the project list: {{message}}
composeList.emptyBody: Open a project you already have (its compose.yaml file) or create a new one. Projects deployed from the terminal show up here automatically.

composeDetail.loadingModel: Reading the file with Docker Compose…
composeDetail.needsValid: Fix the file first: Compose rejects it
composeDetail.registerHint: Keep the project in the list even if its containers are removed
composeDetail.unregisterHint: Only removes it from the list: Docker and the files are not touched
composeDetail.gone: Project “{{name}}” no longer has containers and is not in the list.
composeDetail.missingFiles: These files cannot be found: {{files}}. You can stop, start, view logs or remove the project; deploying it needs the files.
composeDetail.noFiles: Docker does not report the files of this project. You can stop, start, view logs or remove it.
composeDetail.invalidConfig: Docker Compose rejects the project configuration:
composeDetail.noConfig: There is no configuration to show (the files are missing).
composeDetail.configHint: Final configuration as Docker Compose understands it (files merged, variables substituted, all profiles).
composeDetail.secretsWarn: The resolved configuration includes variable values (for example, passwords from the .env file). It is only shown in this window and is not stored in the activity panel.

composeOps.none: No operation has been run on this project yet.
composeOps.dropped_one: {{count}} old line was discarded to limit memory use.
composeOps.dropped_other: {{count}} old lines were discarded to limit memory use.
composeOps.stoppedNote: Docker Compose was interrupted. Whatever it had already done (containers created, images pulled…) is kept.
composeOps.upBody: Creates or updates the project containers, networks and volumes and leaves them running (docker compose up --detach).
composeOps.allServices: With no selection every service is deployed (except those in inactive profiles).
composeOps.someServices: Only the chosen services and the ones they need (depends_on).
composeOps.profilesHint: Services with a profile are only deployed if you enable their profile or pick them above.
composeOps.buildHint: For services with build: (otherwise they are only built if the image does not exist).
composeOps.forceRecreate: Recreate containers even if they have not changed
composeOps.removeOrphansHint: From services that are no longer in the file.
composeOps.downBody_one: {{count}} project container and its networks will be stopped and removed (docker compose down). Volumes and images are kept unless you say otherwise.
composeOps.downBody_other: The {{count}} project containers and their networks will be stopped and removed (docker compose down). Volumes and images are kept unless you say otherwise.
composeOps.downVolumes: Also remove the project's named volumes
composeOps.downVolumesUnknown: The ones declared in the file (or labelled with the project).
composeOps.downVolumesWarn: Data stored in those volumes will be lost permanently.

imagesHint.local: Removes images without a custom tag (the ones Compose builds).
imagesHint.all: Removes every image used by the services, including pulled ones.

composeOps.downSure: I understand the project containers and networks will be removed

composeAdd.title: Open project
composeAdd.body: Choose the project's compose.yaml file. If it uses several files (for example a base file and an override), add them in the order they are merged.
composeAdd.order: They are merged in this order: later files override earlier ones.
composeAdd.name: Project name (optional)
composeAdd.namePh: the one set by the file or folder
composeAdd.nameHint: If left empty, the name Docker Compose decides is used (the file's name: or the folder name).
composeAdd.badName: Only lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter or digit.

composeFile.hint: Saving first validates the content with Docker Compose (without saving it). The file is not overwritten if another program changed it in the meantime.
composeFile.readOnly: You do not have permission to modify this file: it is shown read-only.
composeFile.conflict: The file has changed on disk since you opened it. Nothing was saved, so those changes are not lost.
composeFile.saveInvalid: Docker Compose rejects this content. You can keep editing or save it anyway.
composeFile.discard: You have unsaved changes in this file.

composeLogs.paused: Paused: logs are not being received

composeNew.title: New project
composeNew.nameHint: If you type a name, it is added to the file (name:) so the terminal uses the same one. Otherwise Docker Compose uses the folder name.
composeNew.exists: This folder already has a Docker Compose file ({{file}}). It is not overwritten.
composeNew.editorHint: compose.yaml will be created in the folder. It is validated with Docker Compose before it is created.

events.search: Search by name, ID, action or image
events.clearViewHint: Only clears the list on screen; saved events are kept.
events.liveOn: Live: changes in Docker appear instantly and refresh the whole application
events.livePaused: Paused: events are still received and the application keeps refreshing
events.liveOff: Not connected to Docker: no events are received
events.liveEmpty: Nothing has happened in Docker in this session yet. Create, start or stop something (also from the terminal) and it will show up here.
events.journalIntro: Events the application received while it was open and connected, including previous sessions (the latest 20,000 are kept). If “To” is empty, up to now.
events.journalOff: Saving is disabled in Settings › Activity: new events are not saved.
events.journalCount: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} matching the filters ({{stored}} saved).
events.journalClearBody: The {{count}} saved events will be deleted from disk. Docker and the operation history are not affected.
events.dockerIntro: Asks Docker for the events it keeps (docker events --since … --until …): it includes what happened while the application was closed, but Docker only keeps the latest 256 events in memory and loses them when it restarts. The filter is applied by Docker.
events.truncated: There are more than 5000 events: the most recent are shown.
events.dockerEmpty: Docker keeps no events in that interval with those filters.

history.intro: Operations the application ran on Docker, including previous sessions (the latest 10,000 are kept). What was done, when and with what result are saved; request bodies, equivalent commands and output are not saved because they may contain passwords or other secrets.
history.off: The history is disabled in Settings › Activity: new operations are not saved.
history.search: Search by operation, resource or error
history.count: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} matching the filters ({{stored}} saved).
history.notKeptBody: The request body, equivalent command and output are only in the activity panel during the session in which it ran.
history.clearBody: The {{count}} saved operations will be deleted from disk. This session's activity panel does not change.

updates.title: Updates
updates.installedLocal: Not installed as a package (local build)
updates.sourceHint: A GitHub repository ("owner/repository") or the https:// address of a JSON file with "version". The application only checks and tells you: it never downloads or installs anything.
updates.onStartHint: One request to the source each time the application opens. Without a connection nothing happens: it is noted here.
updates.onStartNoSource: First enter where releases are published.
updates.newer: A new version is available: {{latest}} (you have {{current}}).
updates.upToDate: You have the latest version ({{current}}; the published one is {{latest}}).
updates.howTo: To update, download the new package and install it with "sudo apt install ./docker-control-center_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb". Your settings and history are kept.
updates.banner: A new version of Docker Control Center is available: {{latest}}.

system.title: System
system.hint: Versions and details of this computer. "Copy" creates a text report for reporting a problem (no projects, variables or credentials).

components.title: Uninstall and components
components.rowHint: What the application installed, what can be removed and what is kept. Nothing changes without your confirmation.
components.intro: Analyzes the packages installed with dpkg and APT to show what Docker Control Center installed and what can be safely removed. Analyzing only queries and simulates: it changes nothing. Docker, your data and your settings are always kept.
components.analyzeHint: Runs dpkg-query, apt-mark, apt-cache and an apt-get simulation, without privileges. It is recorded in the activity panel.
components.unsupported: This system does not use dpkg and APT: selective uninstall is only available on Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives.
components.notPackaged: Docker Control Center is not installed as a .deb package (for example, it runs built from source): there is nothing to uninstall with APT.

history.notFound: The APT history does not show how the application was installed (for example, it was installed with dpkg -i or the history has been rotated). For safety, no dependency is offered for removal: all are kept as of uncertain origin.
history.unreadable: The APT history (/var/log/apt/history.log) cannot be read. For safety, no dependency is offered for removal.

components.noneRemovable: None: all dependencies are used by other programs, were already installed or it cannot be safely determined who installed them.
components.presetAll: Docker Control Center and the removable dependencies

class.own: The application package. Removing it does not delete your settings or your data.
class.removable: APT installed them automatically together with the application and no other package needs them.
class.shared: They were installed with the application, but other packages need them: removing them would break those packages.
class.manual: They are marked as explicitly installed (by you or by another program): they are not removed.
class.preExisting: They were installed before the application: they are not removed.
class.uncertain: It cannot be safely determined who installed them: they are kept.
class.protected: Essential system, package management or Docker packages: they are never removed.

components.externalHint: The application uses them, but they are not its own: they are always kept, even if you uninstall the application.
components.dataHint: Your settings and your data are kept. Nothing in Docker is touched either: images, containers, networks, volumes and Compose projects. If you want to delete these folders, do it manually.
components.fullSimulation: APT simulation of the full uninstall
components.fullSimulationHint: What APT would remove if you uninstalled the application with --auto-remove. It may include packages that were already unneeded before; only those installed with the application are offered here.
components.extra: APT would also remove: {{list}}. You cannot continue; review the selection.
components.elevationHint: The system will ask for the administrator password (pkexec) only for this command. If you cancel, nothing is removed.
components.noElevation: pkexec is not installed: the application cannot request permissions. Run this command yourself in a terminal.
components.keptNote: Docker Engine, Docker CLI, Docker Compose, your data and your settings are kept. Purge is not used.
components.selfNote: The application itself is uninstalled: close it when finished.
components.doneSelf: Docker Control Center is no longer installed: close the application.

help.title: Help and documentation
help.rowHint: A guide to every feature, without leaving the application.

errorCodes.engine_timeout: Docker did not respond in time.
errorCodes.engine_pathNotAllowed: For security, only .yml or .yaml files are opened, and not inside hidden folders (such as ~/.ssh) or system folders (such as /etc), nor links to them.
errorCodes.ipc_unavailable: The interface is running outside the desktop application.
errorCodes.updates_invalidSource: Invalid source: enter a GitHub "owner/repository" or an https:// address.
errorCodes.updates_insecureSource: Only https:// addresses are accepted (or http:// to this same computer).
errorCodes.packages_cancelled: Authentication was cancelled: nothing has been uninstalled.
errorCodes.packages_denied: Administrator permissions were not granted: nothing has been uninstalled.
errorCodes.packages_busy: An uninstall is already in progress.
errorCodes.packages_notInstalled: The application is not installed as a .deb package: there is nothing to uninstall with APT.
errorCodes.engine_risksNotAccepted: The configuration has risks to the host that have not been accepted.

commit.title: Create image from {{name}}
commit.intro: A new image is created from the current state of the container's file system (docker commit). The container is not modified.
commit.author: Author (optional)
commit.notIncludedTitle: The image does not include volumes or mounted folders
commit.notIncluded: Only the container's writable layer is saved (the files it changed outside its mounts). The data in these mounts is not part of the image:
commit.excludedList: Mounts not included in the image
commit.noMounts: This container has no mounts: its whole file system is saved.
commit.envIncluded: The image also stores the container's configuration, including its environment variables (even those holding passwords or tokens). Don't push it to a registry if it contains secrets.
commit.running: The container is running. Its processes are not stopped.
commit.pause: Pause the container while the image is created (recommended)
commit.pauseHint: Docker freezes it for a few seconds so the image is consistent, then resumes it. It does not serve requests during that time.
commit.noPauseHint: It is not interrupted, but the image may include half-written files.
commit.replace: Use this name for the new image
commit.replaceHint: The previous image is not deleted: it loses this name (becomes untagged) and its containers keep working.
commit.failed: The image could not be created: {{message}}
commit.loadError: The container could not be read: {{message}}
commit.replaced: The previous image ({{id}}) is kept untagged.

edit.title: Edit configuration of {{name}}
edit.loadError: The container configuration could not be read: {{message}}
edit.tabHasErrors: Some fields in this section need fixing

h.description: Internal note; stored in the container's dcc.description label.
h.backups: Original containers kept when this one was recreated. They are stopped and share the same volumes.
h.networks: Connecting and disconnecting networks is applied immediately, without recreating the container.
h.connect: Pick an existing network; in the next step you can set aliases or a fixed IP.
h.mounts: Host paths or volumes and the path inside the container.
h.env: The container's own variables. Those from the image are inherited anyway.
h.ports: Mapping between host ports and container ports.
h.resources: Docker updates these limits without restarting the container.
h.limitRemoval: Removing a limit (leaving the field empty) cannot be done with docker update: it requires recreating the container.
h.advanced: Docker does not allow changing these options on an existing container.
h.duplicateInstead: To change them, create a new container based on this one:

recreateNote.mounts: Changing mounts requires recreating the container. Volumes and folders are never deleted: a mount you remove is just no longer attached.
recreateNote.ports: Changing ports requires recreating the container. Before applying, the app checks that no other container uses them.

edit.anonymousVolumes: Anonymous volumes that will be mounted again with the same contents: {{names}}
edit.secretsWarning: Variable values can be seen with docker inspect and from inside the container. The app hides those that look secret (passwords, tokens, keys) and never stores them in the activity panel.
edit.imageEnvHint: They come from the image and are inherited; if you define one here with the same name, yours takes precedence.
edit.portsNotApplicable: With the “{{mode}}” network mode Docker does not publish ports.
edit.hostLimits: This computer: {{cpus}} CPUs and {{memory}} of memory.
edit.networkModeSpecial: This container uses the “{{mode}}” network mode: Docker does not allow connecting it to or disconnecting it from networks.
edit.noNetworks: It is not connected to any network.
edit.aliasesRestriction: Docker does not allow changing the aliases or the IP of an existing connection: disconnect the network and connect it again with the new values. The default bridge network has no aliases.
edit.pendingDirect_one: {{count}} pending change. It is applied directly, without recreating the container.
edit.pendingDirect_other: {{count}} pending changes. They are applied directly, without recreating the container.
edit.pendingRecreate_one: {{count}} pending change. It requires recreating the container.
edit.pendingRecreate_other: {{count}} pending changes. At least one requires recreating the container.
edit.fixFirst: Fix the highlighted fields before continuing
edit.restoreBody: The backup is named {{original}} again and started. The container that has that name now is stopped and set aside under another name.
edit.restoreSafe: No container, volume or image is deleted. If the backup does not start, everything goes back to how it was.
edit.removeBackupBody: Only the backup container is deleted (and anything it wrote outside its mounts). Its volumes are not touched: the current container uses them.
edit.rolledBack: The original container is back, with its name and state.
edit.rollbackFailed: The previous state could not be fully restored. Check the steps below.
edit.rollbackFailedHelp: Your data is still there: no volume, folder or image has been deleted, and the original container exists (under its name or the backup name). You can restore it from the General section.
edit.nothingChanged: The container has not been modified.
edit.planError: The changes could not be compared: {{message}}
edit.hasErrors: Some fields must be fixed before applying:

reason.labelsImmutable: Labels cannot be changed on an existing container.
reason.limitRemoval: Docker cannot remove a limit with docker update.

edit.keptRest: The rest of the configuration (image, command, user, networks, unchanged mounts and other options) is kept as is.

plan.backup: It is renamed to {{backup}} and kept as a backup.
plan.create: A new container named {{name}} is created, with the image {{image}} and the full configuration including your changes.
plan.startVerify: It is started and checked to keep running for a few seconds.
plan.verifyStopped: The app checks that Docker created it correctly. It stays stopped, like the original.
plan.rollback: If anything fails, the new container is deleted and the original gets its name and state back.

edit.dataPromise: No volume, folder or image is deleted. Volumes and folders are mounted again in the new container with the same contents.
edit.interruption: The service will be interrupted during the recreation (usually a few seconds).

blocker.state: The container is “{{status}}”. Stop or resume it before recreating it.
blocker.autoRemove: The container was created with “remove when stopped” (--rm): stopping it would make Docker delete it, so it could not be kept as a backup. It cannot be recreated safely.
blocker.composeManaged: The container belongs to the Compose project “{{project}}”. Change it in the Compose file and redeploy: if it were recreated here, Compose would replace it again.
blocker.swarmManaged: The container is managed by a Swarm service. Change the service instead of the container.
blocker.imageMissing: The image {{image}} is no longer available on this computer: without it the new container cannot be created. Pull it first.
blocker.configUnreadable: The full container configuration could not be read ({{detail}}), so it cannot be kept safely.

edit.risksTitle: Before continuing, confirm that you understand these risks:

risk.writableLayer: The container has {{size}} written outside its volumes. Those files are not carried over to the new container (they stay in the backup).
risk.writableLayerUnknown: It could not be determined whether the container has files written outside its volumes. If it does, they are not carried over to the new container (they stay in the backup).
risk.dependents: These containers use this container's network ({{containers}}) and will lose that connection until you recreate them.
risk.mountDetached: No longer mounted: {{mounts}}. Their contents are not deleted.
risk.imageTagMoved: The tag {{image}} now points to a different image. The new container will use the same image as the original (by its ID), not the new one.

riskHint.writableLayer: If you need them, first create an image from this container or move them to a volume.

notice.macUnknown: The container is stopped and Docker does not show its MAC address: the new container will get a new one. If you set a fixed MAC, start the container before recreating it so it can be kept.
notice.macLegacy: This Docker version cannot keep the MAC address when recreating: the new container will get a new one.

edit.keepMacHint: Tick this if you set a fixed MAC (--mac-address). Docker does not tell whether a MAC is fixed or assigned automatically.
edit.finalConfig: View the final configuration of the new container
edit.confirmRecreate: I have reviewed the changes and want to recreate {{name}}
edit.blockedHint: The recreation cannot be done safely (see the reasons)
edit.confirmHint: Confirm the risks and the recreation to continue
edit.doneRecreated: {{name}} has been recreated with the changes and is working correctly.
edit.backupKept: The original container is kept, stopped, as {{backup}}. You can restore or delete it from the General section.

step.update: Update resources and restart policy (docker update)
step.backup: Set the original aside as a backup
step.disconnect: Disconnect a network the original no longer had
step.rollbackRemove: Undo: delete the new container (not its volumes)

servers.notConnectedBody: This server is not connected. Connect to see and manage its Docker; until then no operation is performed on it.
servers.listHint: Disconnecting or deleting a server never touches its containers, images, networks or volumes: they stay on the server as they are.
servers.keyringNotice: {{name}}: the system secure store could not be used ({{message}}). The credential is only valid for this session.
servers.groupWarning: Being a member of the server's docker group is equivalent to root access on that server. Decide with its administrator whether that is acceptable; rootless Docker is the safer alternative.
servers.noAutoFix: The application does not install Docker, change permissions, modify the SSH configuration or open ports on the server: these steps are for you or its administrator to review.

empty.title: No remote servers yet
empty.body: Add a Docker server you can reach over SSH. The connection uses the system SSH client, verifies the server identity and never exposes Docker on the network.

authHint.agent: Uses the keys loaded in the system SSH agent and your ~/.ssh configuration. This is the recommended option.
authHint.key: Uses a private key without a passphrase. Only its path is stored: the key is never copied or read.
authHint.keyPassphrase: Uses a passphrase-protected private key. The passphrase is asked for when connecting and only stored if you ask, in the system secure store.
authHint.password: Not recommended. The password is asked for when connecting and only stored if you ask, in the system secure store. Use keys whenever you can.

dockerHint.default: The Docker the server's docker client uses by default (DOCKER_HOST, context or system socket).
dockerHint.socket: A specific Unix socket on the server, for example the rootless Docker one.
dockerHint.context: A Docker context defined on the server.

hints.name: How it will appear in the application, for example “Production”.
hints.host: DNS name, IPv4 or IPv6 address, or an alias from ~/.ssh/config.
hints.keyPath: The key stays where it is. For example ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.
hints.proxyJump: Format user@host:port (a single hop). Its identity is confirmed by its fingerprint, like the server's, and it must accept your key or SSH agent: passwords are not supported on the jump host and it never receives the server's password.

issues.nameInvalid: The name is too long or contains invalid characters.
issues.hostInvalid: Invalid host: use a name, an IP or an alias without spaces or special characters.
issues.portInvalid: The port must be between 1 and 65535.
issues.socketInvalid: Enter a valid absolute socket path.
issues.proxyJumpChain: Only one jump host is supported: the app checks its identity and the target's.

editor.fixFirst: Review the highlighted fields before continuing.
editor.keyNeverCopied: The application never copies your private key: ssh reads it from its path when connecting.
editor.secretWhen: The passphrase or password is asked for when connecting. If you choose to remember it, it is stored encrypted in the system secure store, never in application files.
editor.secretStored: A credential is saved in the system secure store.

test.intro: Checks step by step that Docker can be managed on the server. It only queries: nothing is changed.
test.secretHint: Only used for this test; it is not stored.
test.readOnly: Only docker --version, docker version and docker system dial-stdio (the API channel) are run on the server.

hostKey.unknownBody: This is the first connection to {{host}} (port {{port}}). Check that this fingerprint belongs to the server before trusting it.
hostKey.changedBody: {{host}} (port {{port}}) presents a different identity from the one confirmed. It may be a reinstall, but also a man-in-the-middle attack. Do not connect until you have checked it.
hostKey.noKey: The server did not present a key that can be shown.
hostKey.howToVerify: To check it, ask the administrator for the server fingerprint or run on the server itself:
hostKey.confirmChanged: I have checked with the server administrator that this new fingerprint is correct.
hostKey.inUserFile: The previous identity is in {{file}}. The application does not modify that file: if you have checked the new fingerprint, remove the old one yourself with:
hostKey.mismatch: The server now presents a different fingerprint from the one shown. Nothing was saved: test the connection again.
hostKey.jumpUnknownBody: This is the first time you go through the jump host {{jump}}. Check that this fingerprint is its own before trusting it.
hostKey.jumpChangedBody: The jump host {{jump}} presents an identity different from the one confirmed. It may be due to a reinstall or a man-in-the-middle attack. Do not continue until you have checked it.

secret.remember: Remember in the system secure store
secret.rememberHint: Stored encrypted by the system (GNOME Keyring, KWallet…). You can delete it when editing the server.
secret.noKeyring: No secure store is available in this session: it will be asked for on every connection. It is never stored in plain text.
secret.passwordDiscouraged: Password authentication is not recommended: SSH keys are more secure.

deleteDialog.title: Delete the profile of {{name}}?
deleteDialog.body: The connection profile, its saved credentials and, if no other profile uses it, the confirmed server identity are removed from the application.
deleteDialog.nothingRemote: Nothing is deleted on the server: its containers, images, networks, volumes and data stay intact.

overview.intro: Each server is queried separately: a slow or unavailable one does not affect the others.

diagnosis.title: Diagnosis of {{name}}
diagnosis.localHint: The detailed diagnosis of this computer is on the Dashboard when there is no connection.

sshMissing.title: There is no SSH client on this computer
sshMissing.body: Managing remote servers requires the ssh program (OpenSSH).

invalidProfile.title: The server profile is not valid

hostUnreachable.title: The server is unreachable
hostUnreachable.body: There is no network route to {{host}}: {{message}}

sshRefused.title: SSH is not answering on the server
sshRefused.body: {{host}} refuses connections on port {{port}}: the SSH service is stopped or listens on another port.

notSsh.title: That port is not SSH
notSsh.body: What answers on {{host}}:{{port}} is not an SSH server.

timeout.title: The server does not answer in time
timeout.body: There was no answer from {{host}}:{{port}} within {{seconds}} seconds. A firewall may be dropping the connection.

hostKeyUnknown.title: Server identity not confirmed
hostKeyUnknown.body: This is the first connection to {{host}}. Confirm its fingerprint ({{type}} {{fingerprint}}) before connecting.

hostKeyChanged.title: The server identity has changed!
hostKeyChanged.body: {{host}} presents a different identity ({{type}} {{fingerprint}}) from the confirmed one. It could be a man-in-the-middle attack. The connection has been stopped.

authFailedKey.title: The key is not accepted
authFailedKey.body: The server does not accept the key for user {{user}}.

authFailedAgent.title: The SSH agent has no accepted key
authFailedAgent.body: The server accepts none of the SSH agent keys for user {{user}}.

authFailedPassword.title: Wrong user or password
authFailedPassword.body: The server does not accept the password for user {{user}}.

passphraseRequired.title: The passphrase is missing
passphraseRequired.body: The key is protected with a passphrase and none is available.

passwordRequired.title: The password is missing
passwordRequired.body: This server uses a password and none is available.

keyUnreadable.title: The private key cannot be found
keyUnreadable.body: {{path}} does not exist or cannot be read.

dockerMissing.title: Docker is not installed on the server
dockerMissing.body: The docker program is not available to the user on {{host}}.

dockerNotRunning.title: Docker is stopped on the server
dockerNotRunning.body: The Docker daemon is not answering on {{host}}: {{message}}

socketDenied.title: No permission to use Docker on the server
socketDenied.body: User {{user}} cannot use the Docker socket on {{host}}: {{message}}

contextMissing.title: That Docker context does not exist
contextMissing.body: The context {{name}} is not defined on {{host}}.

notDocker.title: That is not Docker
notDocker.body: What answers on the given socket of {{host}} is not Docker Engine: {{message}}

apiTooOld.title: Incompatible Docker version
apiTooOld.body: {{host}} has API {{version}}; the application needs at least {{minimum}} (Docker 20.10).

connectionLost.title: The connection was lost
connectionLost.body: The SSH connection to {{host}} was cut.

jumpHostKeyUnknown.title: Jump host identity not confirmed
jumpHostKeyUnknown.body: This is the first connection through the jump host {{jump}}. Confirm its fingerprint ({{type}} {{fingerprint}}) before continuing.

jumpHostKeyChanged.title: The jump host identity has changed
jumpHostKeyChanged.body: The jump host {{jump}} presents an identity different from the confirmed one. It may be a man-in-the-middle attack: do not continue until you have checked it.

jumpAuthFailed.title: The jump host does not accept the key
jumpAuthFailed.body: {{jump}} accepted no key and not the SSH agent. Only a key or the agent is supported on the jump host; the target server's password is never sent to it.

jumpFromSshConfig.title: Jump defined in ~/.ssh/config
jumpFromSshConfig.body: Your ~/.ssh/config routes {{host}} through {{via}}. With a password or passphrase the app does not connect that way, because that jump would not have the app's checks. Set the jump host in the profile.

fix.editProfile: Edit the server and fix its details.
fix.checkName: Check that the name is spelled correctly or use the IP address.
fix.resolveName: Check whether this computer resolves the name.
fix.checkNetwork: Check the network, VPN or firewall between this computer and the server.
fix.sshdStatus: Check that the SSH service is running.
fix.checkFirewall: Check that no firewall drops connections to that port.
fix.raiseTimeout: If the network is slow, raise the connection timeout in the advanced options.
fix.verifyFingerprint: Ask the administrator for the server fingerprint or check it on the server itself.
fix.trustIfMatches: If it matches exactly, confirm it.
fix.doNotConnect: Do not connect or type passwords until you know why it changed.
fix.askAdmin: Ask the administrator whether the server was reinstalled or its keys changed.
fix.removeUserKey: If the new fingerprint is correct, remove the old one from your ~/.ssh/known_hosts (the application does not modify that file).
fix.replaceInApp: If the new fingerprint is correct, replace it explicitly.

why.runtimeSocket: With the socket, anyone can create a privileged container and control the whole host.
why.hostRoot: The container can read, and with write access change, any file on the host.
why.credentials: It exposes passwords, keys or tokens of the host or its users.
why.systemDir: It lets the container read or change the host configuration.
why.systemBinaries: It lets the container replace host programs or libraries.
why.capability: Each added capability extends what the container can do with the kernel.
why.privileged: No isolation: devices, kernel and every capability.
why.networkHost: It sees every service on the host, including those only listening on 127.0.0.1.
why.hostNamespace: It breaks part of the isolation between the container and the host.
why.securityOpt: It turns off a kernel protection that limits what a compromised process can do.
why.device: Direct access to the device, bypassing file permissions.
why.cgroupParent: Resource limits are no longer managed like the other containers.
why.portAllInterfaces: Other machines on the network can connect, and with Docker the firewall usually does not block it.
why.rootUser: If the process is compromised, the attacker is root inside the container and escaping is easier. With rootless Docker or userns-remap the risk is lower.
why.writableRootfs: An attacker can drop programs or change the configuration inside the container.
why.noMemoryLimit: A bug or an attack can use up all the host's memory.
why.noCpuLimit: One process can take all the CPU and slow everything else down.
why.noPidsLimit: A fork bomb can exhaust the host's processes.
why.noNewPrivileges: setuid programs can gain privileges inside the container.
why.imageOld: An old image usually has vulnerabilities that newer versions have fixed.
why.imageRootUser: Containers created from it run as root unless another user is given. With rootless Docker or userns-remap the risk is lower.

fix.runtimeSocket: Remove the socket. If it is really needed, use a socket proxy with limited permissions or rootless Docker.
fix.hostRoot: Mount only the folder it needs, read-only if possible.
fix.credentials: Mount only the specific file it needs, or pass the secret with Docker secrets.
fix.systemDir: Mount only what is needed, read-only.
fix.systemBinaries: Mount it read-only or not at all.
fix.capability: Remove the capability if it is not needed; start from --cap-drop ALL and add only the essential ones.
fix.privileged: Remove --privileged and add only the capabilities or devices it needs.
fix.networkHost: Use a Docker network and publish only the ports you need.
fix.hostNamespace: Remove the option unless the container really needs it (e.g. diagnostic tools).
fix.securityOpt: Remove the option; if a profile blocks something, write a custom profile instead of turning it off.
fix.device: Pass only the specific device it needs, or none.
fix.cgroupParent: Remove cgroup_parent unless you manage control groups yourself.
fix.portAllInterfaces: If you only use it on this computer, publish it on 127.0.0.1.
fix.rootUser: Set an unprivileged user (--user, or user: in Compose) or use an image that already has one.
fix.writableRootfs: Use --read-only (read_only: true) with a tmpfs or a volume for what it has to write.
fix.noMemoryLimit: Set a memory limit (--memory or mem_limit).
fix.noCpuLimit: Set a CPU limit (--cpus or cpus).
fix.noPidsLimit: Set a process limit (--pids-limit or pids_limit).
fix.imageOld: Pull or build a recent version of the image and recreate the container.
fix.imageRootUser: Use an image with an unprivileged user (USER in the Dockerfile) or pass --user when creating the container.

backup.intro: Back up volumes, databases (with the engine's own dump tool) and the configuration of containers, Compose projects and the application. Each backup has a manifest with the SHA-256 checksum of every file; files are saved with 0600 permissions. Not encrypted: keep your backups somewhere safe.
